paragraphs.text: Being parted and being near happen at once. Though parted from the Ruler, though it be a mere instant, I burn thickly all the while: may I be ground for His glance. In parting-pithed passing — by You, dear Master — may I be ever unparted, though parted from the world.

And here is the truth that gets shown and won. Body, speech, mind: wherever I go with them, all is You alone — may this highest truth stand full for me, ever. Thought-free as You, great-bliss-full as You: so may my praise-making match, and only match. Held by You, seeing thing and thing made by You: may I roam longing-free, joy-brimmed. Lord, may I see the all-world full of Your being — with that alone content. Then no more wearing out. Melting in You alone like cloud-shreds in sky: may things shine for me, ever, step by step stainless. Self-light outspread, shattering the endless dark-train: shine for me ever, some jewel of Your being, from Your middle. What ground do You not rule? What could there be that is not Your body? Weary — thereby, by no effort, may I win You everywhere.
